direction_as_read: Mixed: olive leaf extract lowered 24-hour systolic pressure in one large trial and improved vital signs in a small COVID-19 trial, while glycemic and anxiety trials found no effect
summary: Three of four products are named Olive Leaf Extract and print olive extract 500 mg with an immune purpose; the fourth is Cardio Health, 500 mg olive extract with a cardiovascular purpose and no plant part in the row read. None prints fruit. In hospitalized COVID-19 patients, olive leaf extract 500 or 1000 mg/day for five days improved primary vital signs versus placebo (36319585). In 621 people treated for hypertension, it lowered 24-hour systolic pressure versus placebo, with no dose in the abstract (40990594). In stage-1 hypertension, EFLA 943 at 1000 mg/day reduced systolic pressure about as much as captopril, with no placebo arm (21036583). In 32 high school athletes, illness incidence did not differ though sick days fell (30744092). A pilot in type 2 diabetes found no significant HbA1c interaction (39818111), and an anxiety pilot that missed its sample size reported no effect (42514151). The stored meta-analysis tested isolated oleuropein, hydroxytyrosol and tyrosol, not an olive extract as printed here.
question_for_clinician: 36319585 meets rule 2 for olive leaf extract at 500 or 1000 mg/day, positive on primary vital signs in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. 21036583 meets rule 2 for EFLA 943 at 1000 mg/day, with a primary systolic reduction similar to captopril and no placebo arm. Should the 3 immune labels get credit from one short inpatient trial, given 30744092 found no difference in illness incidence? Should Cardio Health get credit from 21036583, and from 40990594 once its dose is read? Agent recommendation: no credit in this review. The labels print no oleuropein amount and no extract name, Cardio Health states no plant part in the row read, 36319585 does not show general immune support, and the dose in 40990594 is not verified. The full text of 40990594 would most help the cardiovascular label.
